newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile seeks bank law passage in January - Aninat.
newsitem.headline: Chile seeks bank law passage in January - Aninat.

text.p: Chile's finance ministry will press Congress to pass a package of new banking regulations known as the Ley de Bancos by the end of January, Finance Minister Eduardo Aninat said.
Aninat said settlement this year of the private banking system's $4.5 billion in debts with the Central Bank has now cleared the way for passage of the Ley de Bancos.
Deputy Finance Minister Manuel Marfan would be pressing Congress for action by the end of the current legislative session on January 31, he said.
''We're stepping on the gas to have the law on new banking business passed by the end of January,'' he said at a breakfast with the Chilean Foreign Correspondents' Association.
''I've given very precise instructions to Manuel Marfan to lead the banking reform issue and that we must have the law governing new banking businesses in hand by January 31,'' said Aninat.
''Of course, it doesn't all depend on him (Marfan). It also depends on congressmen helping to speed up the discussion,'' he said.

The bill, bottled up in Congress for at least two years, sets terms and regulations for a wide array of new overseas and domestic financial services which Chilean banks have been hankering to get into for years.
It went nowhere this year while the Central Bank and seven private institutions hammered out rescheduling deals for the private banks' debts incurred during Chile's last big banking crisis in 1981.
The new law gives ''more freedom but also more supervision'' for banking services, said Aninat, ''because we love being mistrustful when we're talking about the banking sector.''
''We need greater flexibility for cross-border investments...but we don't believe in pure deregulation, in the same way we don't believe in pure control'' over banking, he said.
